prompt: Users in Australia wait longer because the server is far away in Europe.
tells: the server is far away in Europe
why: Messages take time to travel long distances and back. That delay is latency.
trap: The server isn't overloaded; it's distant.

prompt: The page makes 40 small requests one after another, and each request waits for the last.
tells: each request waits for the last
why: Each trip adds delay, and many trips in a row add up. That's latency.
trap: The server may cope fine; the waiting is in the trips.

prompt: A gamer's ping shows 180 ms, so actions feel delayed.
why: Ping measures the round trip time. High latency makes actions feel slow.

prompt: Moving copies of the site closer to users cut load times in Asia.
tells: closer to users cut load times
why: Shorter distance means shorter round trips. The problem being solved is latency.
trap: Caching is the method; latency is what it reduces.

prompt: On a satellite connection, every page feels sluggish even though the download speed is good.
tells: even though the download speed is good
why: Bandwidth can be high while each trip still takes long. That's latency.
trap: Speed of download isn't the issue; round trips are.

prompt: Combining five calls into one made the app feel twice as fast.
why: Fewer round trips means less waiting. That's reducing latency.
trap: The API is involved, but the gain is fewer trips.
